ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in quadrilateral $ABCD$, $AB \parallel CD$, $AB = 5$, $DC = 11$, and the sum of $AD$ and $BC$ is $12$. Points $E$, $F$, and $G$ are the midpoints of $BD$, $AC$, and $DC$ respectively. What is the perimeter of $\triangle EFG$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:}

As shown in the figure, extend AE and continue it to intersect CD at point K,\\
since AB$\parallel$CD,\\
it follows that $\angle$BAE$=\angle$DKE and $\angle$ABD$=\angle$EDK,\\
since points E, F, G are the midpoints of BD, AC, DC respectively.\\
It follows that BE$=$DE,\\
so, triangle AEB is congruent to triangle KED (AAS),\\
thus, DK$=$AB, AE$=$EK,\\
therefore, EF is the midline of triangle ACK,\\
therefore, EF$=\frac{1}{2}$CK$=\frac{1}{2}$(DC$-$AB),\\
since EG is the midline of triangle BCD,\\
it follows that EG$=$BC,\\
also, since FG is the midline of triangle ACD,\\
it follows that FG$=$AD,\\
hence, EG+GF$=\frac{1}{2}$(AD+BC),\\
since AD+BC$=12$, AB$=5$, DC$=11$,\\
thus, EG+GF$=6$, FE$=3$,\\
therefore, the perimeter of triangle EFG is $6+3=\boxed{9}$.
